label: mid-input steps (t=3-6) after several of {0,y,b,q,l,g,1}
explanation: Fires almost only during the original-input phase at positions 3-6 (peak t=5; 97% of mass at t=3..6), a little on the <DEL> step, never in the copy phase or at t<2. Within that window, it is driven by the input history: rate is highest when earlier inputs (prev_tok, prev2_tok) include 0, y, b, q, l (also g, 1), and when the current input is 0, w, 1 or y; more digits in the sequence raise the rate. Counting how many of {0,y,b,q,l,g,1} came before gives a graded signal, and top activations come from sequences dense in these tokens. The position window alone has 97% mass recall but only 4% precision; the token-history condition improves precision but loses recall (dev F1 about 0.38), so the token dependence looks like a distributed weighted sum that one simple set does not capture.
